QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r2.claim: Qatada explains that the final destination is to the Lord, paralleling the statement that the final end is to Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r6.claim: Everyone returns to God and cannot appeal to another being to escape accountability; God’s decisions are final.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p67/r6.anchor: Everyone will be brought before God and all decisions of God will be final and irrevocable.

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.claim: This section then turns to perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.anchor: transitions into a discussion of the perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham

RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r1.claim: The common reading opens the hamza and coordinates this statement with the preceding “that”; a reading with kasra treats it as an independent sentence.
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r1.anchor: القراءة المشهورة فتح الهمزة على العطف على ما ، يعني أن هذا أيضا في الصحف

RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r2.claim: The well-known interpretation is resurrection: everyone returns to God, where the grateful are rewarded and the ungrateful punished; this answers when the recompense mentioned just before occurs.
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r2.anchor: بيان المعاد أي للناس بين يدي الله وقوف

RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r3.claim: The verse can prove God’s existence: contingent things require a cause, and tracing causes cannot end in another contingent thing, so reason must terminate at the necessary existent, the source of all existence.
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r3.anchor: إذا نظرت إلى الموجودات الممكنة لا تجد لها بدا من موجد

RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet through Ubayy says, “No reflection on the Lord”; al-Rāzī reads this as reaching the necessary existent, whose existence is not caused.
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r4.anchor: المروي عن أبي بن كعب أنه قال عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( وأن إلى ربك المنتهى

RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r5.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that when the Lord is mentioned, one should stop; al-Rāzī says this can support his account of the final terminus.
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r5.anchor: وقال أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( إذا ذكر الرب فانتهوا )

RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r6.claim: Some people extend the necessary-existence interpretation to every verse about return or ascent, including 35:10; al-Rāzī says that reading is not apparent in some such verses, though it is clear here.
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r6.anchor: حتى قيل : { إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب } ( فاطر : 10 ) بهذا المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r7.claim: The verse also indicates divine unity: the terminus is necessary existence precisely as necessary; if there were two necessary beings, neither could be the final terminus, and the argument collapses to one.
RAZI-FULL:v29p16/r7.anchor: فلو كان واجبان في الوجود لكان كل واحد قبل المنتهى لأن المجموع قبله الواجب فهو المنتهى

RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r1.claim: The addressee may be any listener or rational person, or specifically the Prophet; these readings shape the verse’s application.
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r1.anchor: في المخاطب وجهان : أحدهما : أنه عام تقديره إلى ربك أيها السامع أو العاقل

RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r2.claim: If addressed generally, the statement is a forceful threat to wrongdoers and encouragement to the righteous, since every listener’s end is before God.
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r2.anchor: فهو تهديد بليغ للمسيء وحث شديد للمحسن

RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r3.claim: If addressed to Muhammad, it validates his religion: he professes the one self-sufficient Lord on whom every contingent being depends, the Lord of lords and cause of causes.
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r3.anchor: لكنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قال : ( ربي الذي هو أحد وصمد ) يحتاج إليه كل ممكن

RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r4.claim: On the Prophet-directed reading, the verse consoles him not to grieve and recalls the assurance that God knows what opponents say and that all return to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r4.anchor: فهو تسلية لقلبه كأنه يقول : لا تحزن فإن المنتهى إلى الله فيكون كقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r5.claim: With a general addressee, the definite article refers to the promised return already stated in revelation and by the Prophet; with the Prophet as addressee, it is generic: every terminus is to the Lord, who is its origin.
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r5.anchor: اللام على الوجه الأول للعهد لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول : أبدا إن مرجعكم إلى الله

RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r6.claim: On the generic reading, human perception begins with outward things and, through deeper reflection, reaches God and stops there.
RAZI-FULL:v29p17/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه نقول : منتهى الإدراكات المدركات ، فإن الإنسان أولا يدرك الأشياء الظاهرة ثم

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.claim: Except verse 46, each verse in 42–50 begins wa anna, continuing the discussion of Moses’ and Abraham’s scriptures in 36–41.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.anchor: Each verse in this passage, except v. 46, begins with wa anna

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.claim: Wa anna may instead be read wa inna, making each instance an independent thought meaning truly, surely, or verily.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.anchor: But wa anna could also be read wa inna, which would make each occurrence mark a new, independent thought

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r3.claim: Unto the Lord evokes Judgment Day, when everyone stands before God.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r3.anchor: Unto thy Lord conveys a sense of the Day of Judgment, when everyone will stand before God.

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r4.claim: Although all created things ultimately return to God, different groups have different ends: the reverent are promised a Garden and disbelievers the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r4.anchor: there are nonetheless disparate ends for various groups, as in 13:35

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r6.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r6.claim: Another understanding takes the ultimate end as a reference to God as the Necessary Being and Source of all beings.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r6.anchor: The ultimate end can also be seen as a reference to God as the One Necessary Being, Who is the Source of all beings (R).

BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r7.claim: The path is one in its unity though paths to God are as numerous as creatures' breaths; they converge at the end, and after death God brings the seeker to his aspiration.
BURSEVI:v9p206#2/r7.anchor: والا فالطرق الى الله بعدد انفاس الخلائق فعند النهاية يحصل الالتقاء ولذا قال تعالى وان الى ربك المنهى

BURSEVI:v9p207/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p207/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p207/r5.claim: Al-muntahā means the end or return: after death all creatures return to God alone for recompense; in truth their beginning and end are both in Him.
BURSEVI:v9p207/r5.anchor: مصدر بمعنى الانتهاء أي انتهاء الخلق في رجوعهم إلى الله تعالى بعد الموت لا إلى غيره

BURSEVI:v9p207/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p207/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p207/r6.claim: This accords with the declaration that all affairs return to God, since no deity exists but Him.
BURSEVI:v9p207/r6.anchor: ألا إلى الله تصير الأمور إذ لا إله إلا هو

BURSEVI:v9p207/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p207/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p207/r7.claim: Rūmī's verses compare God to a boundless sea before which all other seas and streams are small.
BURSEVI:v9p207/r7.anchor: كان يكى درياست بى غور وكران جمله درياها وسبلى يش آن

BURSEVI:v9p207/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p207/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v9p207/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says whoever begins from God ends with Him; knowing divine lordship removes temptation and leaves no will besides God's choice.
BURSEVI:v9p207/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : من كان منه مبدأه كان إليه منتهاه وإذا وصل العبد إلى معرفة الربوبية

BURSEVI:v9p207/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p207/r9.speaker: الحسين
BURSEVI:v9p207/r9.claim: Asked to define unity, al-Ḥusayn says it is to hold God as the cause of all: effects begin from Him, return to Him, and disappear while their cause remains.
BURSEVI:v9p207/r9.anchor: قيل للحسين ما التوحيد قال أن تعتقد أنه معلل الكل لقوله هو الأول

BURSEVI:v9p207/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p207/r10.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v9p207/r10.claim: Some authorities call God the cause of causes as proof of unity for those without unveiling; Bursevī says this unscriptural title must not be used to invoke or describe Him.
BURSEVI:v9p207/r10.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : من أدل دليل على توحيد الله تعالى عند من لا كشف عنده كونه تعالى عند النظار والفلاسفة علة العلل

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r6.claim: Al-muntaha is an infinitive noun meaning ending; stated absolutely, it conveys every kind of ending.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r6.anchor: المنتهى مصدر ميمي بمعنى الانتهاء وقد أطلق إطلاقا فيفيد مطلق الانتهاء

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r7.claim: All beings and their effects, as well as every system of governance, ultimately depend on God, directly or through causes; God creates beings and the relations among them.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r7.anchor: فما في الوجود من شيء موجود إلا وينتهي في وجوده وآثار وجوده إلى الله سبحانه بلا واسطة أو مع الواسطة

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r8.claim: The verse establishes God’s absolute lordship: all governance ends with Him, including both the origin of things through creation and their return through resurrection.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r8.anchor: والآية تثبت الربوبية المطلقة لله سبحانه بإنهاء كل تدبير وكل التدبير إليه وتشمل انتهاء الأشياء إليه من حيث البدء

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r9.claim: The restricted interpretation that the verse means only the creation’s return to God on Judgment Day is too narrow.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r9.anchor: يظهر ضعف ما قيل في تفسير الآية إن المراد بذلك رجوع الخلق إليه سبحانه يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r10.claim: The interpretation that the final destination is only God’s reward and punishment unnecessarily restricts the verse.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r10.anchor: وكذا ما قيل إن المعنى أن إلى ثواب ربك وعقابه آخر الأمر

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r11.claim: The interpretation that people’s endpoint is only God’s reckoning is too restrictive.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r11.anchor: وكذا ما قيل المعنى أن إلى حساب ربك منتهاهم

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r12.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r12.claim: The interpretation that thought terminates and stops before God also narrows the verse without textual restriction.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r12.anchor: وكذا ما قيل إليه سبحانه ينتهي الأفكار وتقف دونه

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r6.claim: Imam al-Sadiq cites the verse and instructs that when speech reaches God, one should stop.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r6.anchor: قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r7.claim: Al-Tabatabai regards the report as an expanded application of the word ‘ending.’
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r7.anchor: أقول وهو من التوسعة في معنى الانتهاء

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r8.claim: Imam al-Baqir warns Ziyad that disputation breeds doubt, cancels deeds, and ruins its practitioner; people who pursued forbidden knowledge became confused, with another version saying they wandered on earth.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r8.anchor: إلى أبي عبيدة الحذاء قال قال أبو جعفر عليه السلام يا زياد إياك والخصومات

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r9.speaker: أبو ذر
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r9.claim: Abu Dharr transmits the Prophet’s instruction to contemplate God’s creation, not God Himself, lest one perish.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r9.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r10.claim: The many reports in both traditions forbidding thought about God are guidance for those unprepared for difficult rational inquiry, whose delving into it risks lasting ruin.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r10.anchor: والنهي إرشادي متعلق بمن لا يحسن الورود في المسائل العقلية العميقة فيكون خوضه فيها تعرضا للهلاك الدائم

TABRISI:53:42-43/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:42-43/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:42-43/r1.claim: The ultimate end is with the Lord: the final destination is His reward and punishment, where action comes to an end.
TABRISI:53:42-43/r1.anchor: يعني وأن إلى ثواب ربك وعقابه آخر الأمر والمنتهى

THALABI:v9p154/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p154/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p154/r4.claim: The end of creation and its return are to God, who will requite creatures for their deeds.
THALABI:v9p154/r4.anchor: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى أي منتهى الخلق ومصيرهم، وهو مجازيهم بأعمالهم

THALABI:v9p154/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p154/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p154/r5.claim: Another view says beneficence begins from God and hopes finally end with Him.
THALABI:v9p154/r5.anchor: وقيل: منه ابتداء المنة وإليه انتهاء الآمال

THALABI:v9p154/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p154/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p154/r6.claim: A report from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb interprets the verse as forbidding speculation about God.
THALABI:v9p154/r6.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله سبحانه: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى قال: «لا فكرة في الله

THALABI:v9p154/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p154/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p154/r7.claim: As corroboration, a Prophetic report says that when God is mentioned, people should stop.
THALABI:v9p154/r7.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إذا ذكر الله عز وجل فانتهوا»

THALABI:v9p154/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p154/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p154/r8.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra urges reflection on creation rather than the Creator, who cannot be encompassed by thought, and describes the vast layers of earth, heavens, and a sea in the seventh heaven.
THALABI:v9p154/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أصحابه وهم يتفكرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r1.claim: The servants’ endpoint and return are to God; this is the exegetes’ interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وأن إلى ربك المنتهى} أي إليه منتهى العباد ومرجعهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r2.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r2.claim: An alternative interpretation attributed to the Prophet says: “No reflection about the Lord.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r2.anchor: وروي تفسير آخر لهذه الآية مرفوعا إلى النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: "لا فكرة في الرب"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r3.claim: A person can think through created things but cannot comprehend God’s knowledge, essence, or modality; God is the endpoint of thought in this respect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r3.anchor: فلا يحيط به علما ولا يدركه بفكرته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r4.speaker: أنس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r4.claim: A report from Anas says the Prophet taught: when God is mentioned, stop.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r5.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r5.claim: The Prophet taught people to reflect on creation and not on the Creator.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r5.anchor: وقال -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: "تفكروا في الخلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p69#3/r6.claim: Al-muntahā means the endpoint or termination.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r7.claim: The final destination and return are to God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r7.anchor: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى } المصير والمرجع

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r16.claim: Everyone ultimately returns to God and is gathered before Him, where complete recompense is realized; He is the First and the Last.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r16.anchor: Bütün halk sonunda dönüp O’na varır, O’nun huzûruna haşr u ihzar olunur, işte o vakit o tam cezâ da hakka’l-yakīn olur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r5.claim: At the end of judgment everyone receives the full recompense for what they did.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r5.anchor: Sözü edilen yargılamanın sonunda herkese yaptıklarının karşılığı tastamam verilecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r6.claim: No one will suffer the slightest injustice, but divine grace and forgiveness remain subject to God’s absolute will; believers should hope without becoming complacent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r6.anchor: ilâhî lutuf ve bağışlama hususu Allah’ın mutlak iradesine bağlıdır; bu konuda mümine düşen, ümitvar olmak, ama buna güvenerek gevşeklik göstermemektir

BURHAN:v2p515/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p515/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p515/r3.claim: The pattern فعلى may be a noun, as in الشورى, الرجعى, and العليا.
BURHAN:v2p515/r3.anchor: وأما فعلى فيكون اسما كالشورى والرجعى قال الله تعالى ﴿ إن إلى ربك الرجعى ﴾

SULAMI:v2p289/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p289/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p289/r1.claim: When a servant reaches knowledge of lordship, every trial turns away and he has no will except what God chooses for him.
SULAMI:v2p289/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : إذا وصل العبد إلى معرفة الربوبية تنحرف عنه كل فتنة ولا يكون له مشيئة غير اختيار الله له

SULAMI:v2p289/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p289/r2.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p289/r2.claim: Husayn defines tawhid as affirming God’s encompassing presence, citing “He is the First”; all contingent things seek their beginning and end from Him, and they vanish while their cause remains.
SULAMI:v2p289/r2.anchor: قيل للحسين : ما التوحيد ؟ فقال : أن يعتقد انه مع الكل بقوله : ﴿ هو الأول ﴾

NAHHAS:v4p276/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r15.claim: Al-muntahā is the accusative noun of anna; as a defective noun, its case ending is not visible.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r15.anchor: في موضع نصب اسم أن إلا أنه مقصور لا يتبين فيه الإعراب

NAHHAS:v4p276/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r16.claim: All creation returns to God, who recompenses their good and bad deeds.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r16.anchor: والمعنى وأن إلى ربك انتهاء جميع خلقه ومصيرهم فيجازيهم بأعمالهم الحسنة والسيئة

SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r1.claim: The common reading opens this hamza and the coordinated ones, understanding all these statements to be in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r1.anchor: العامة على فتح هذه الهمزة وما عطف عليها بمعنى: أن الجميع في صحف موسى وإبراهيم.

SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r2.speaker: أبو السمال
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r2.claim: Abu al-Sammāl reads the coordinated hamzas with kasra as independent beginnings.
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال بالكسر في الجميع على الابتداء

SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r3.claim: أضحك وأبكى and the following oppositions form antithesis: opposites, contraries, or things incompatible in some respect.
SAMIN-DURR:53:42/r3.anchor: هذا يسميه البيانيون الطباق والتضاد، وهو نوع من البديع

ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r4.claim: The final return is to the Lord; this teaching too is found in Abraham's and Moses' scrolls.
ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r4.anchor: أي إليه المرجع، وهذا كله في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n34/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n34/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n34/r1.claim: The ultimate limit or goal encompasses the universe's beginning and end in time and space, and is both the source from which all proceeds and the destination to which all returns.
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n34/r1.anchor: the utmost limit" or "goal", circumscribing the beginning and the end of the universe both in time and in space

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r1.claim: All creatures end and return to God alone at the Resurrection; no other has an independent or shared role in that final return.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r1.anchor: أي إن انتهاء الخلق ورجوعهم إليه تعالى لا إلى غيره سبحانه استقلالا ولا اشتراكا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r2.claim: Several commentators gloss the destination as God's reckoning, reward in Paradise, or punishment in the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r2.anchor: ولهذا قال غير واحد : أي إلى حساب ربك أو إلى ثوابه تعالى من الجنة وعقابه من النار

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r3.claim: Another interpretation makes God the limit of thought: inquiry into realities stops when it reaches the divine essence and attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r3.anchor: وقيل : المعنى أنه عز وجل منتهى الأفكار فلا تزال الأغكار تسير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r4.claim: A report from Ubayy ibn Ka'b attributes to the Prophet the statement that there is no thinking about the Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r4.anchor: وأيد بما أخرجه البغوي عن أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال في الآية : لا فكرة في الرب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r5.speaker: سفيان الثوري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r5.claim: Abu al-Shaykh transmits from Sufyan al-Thawri a Prophetic report: when the Lord is mentioned, stop there.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r5.anchor: وأخرجه أبو الشيخ في العظمة عن سفيان الثوري وروي عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إذا ذكر الرب فانتهوا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet told people contemplating God to contemplate creation instead, since they could not encompass the Creator.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r6.anchor: ابن ماجة عن ابن عباس قال : مر النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على قوم يتفكرون في الله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r7.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r7.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying to contemplate God's creation and not God, lest one perish.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r7.anchor: عن أبي ذر قالأ : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : تفكروا في خلق الله ولا تفكروا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the passage supports those who hold that God's essence cannot be known in its full reality; he notes that most transmitted proofs point this way.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r8.anchor: أكثر الأدلة النقلية على عدم الوقوع

ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r9.speaker: أبو السمال
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r9.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads inna with kasra here and in the following instances, treating these clauses as disconnected from what precedes and not among the scrolls' contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p68/r9.anchor: أبو السمال وإن بالكسر هنا وفيما بعدعلى أن الجمل منقطعة عما قبلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r4.claim: All creation ends with God and returns to Him, and He recompenses them for their deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r4.anchor: {وأن إلى ربك المنتهى} أي: منتهى الخلق ومصيرهم إليه، وهو مجازيهم بأعمالهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r5.claim: Another explanation says beneficence begins from God and hopes ultimately end with Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r5.anchor: وقيل: منه ابتداء المنة وإليه انتهاء الآمال.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r6.claim: The Prophet, reporting Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's explanation, says there is no reflection about God; the report gives no grading.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية، عن أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: "وأن إلى ربك المنتهى"، قال: "لا فكرة في الرب"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r7.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says to reflect on creation rather than the Creator, since thought cannot encompass Him; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p417/r7.anchor: وهذا مثل ما روي عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا: "تفكروا في الخلق ولا تتفكروا في الخالق" (6) فإنه لا تحيط به الفكرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r4.claim: All creatures end with their return to their Lord.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r4.anchor: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى } انتهاء الخلائق ورجوعهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r5.claim: A kasra reading breaks this clause from what is in the Scriptures, as it does the clauses that follow.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:39-46/r5.anchor: وقرىء بالكسر على أنه منقطع عما في الصحف

BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r4.claim: All creatures finally return to God bodily through resurrection and in their deeds, knowledge, hopes, and affairs; their destination in place and time, like their beginning, is from Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r4.anchor: { المنتهى * } أي الانتهاء برجوع الخلائق حسا بالبعث ومعنى بالعمل والعلم , وإسناد الأمور وإرسال الآمال , ومكان رجوعهم وزمانه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r5.claim: The verse closes the chain of proof: appointed angels may see deeds, but the ultimate and more awe-inspiring witness is the supreme King Himself.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r5.anchor: وكان الرائي كلما كان أكثر كان الأمر أهول , وكان رؤية الملك الأعظم أخوف , قال عاطفا على { لا تزر } مبينا بحروف الغاية

BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r6.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, through Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, a Prophetic report: “There is no reflection on the Lord.”
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r6.anchor: روى البغوي من طريق أبي جعفر الرازي عن أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الآية قال ( لا فكرة في الرب )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r7.claim: A marfuʿ report from Abu Hurayra says to reflect on creation, not the Creator, because thought cannot encompass Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p330/r7.anchor: قال : ومثل هذا ما روي عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه مرفوعا : ( تفكروا في الخلق ولا تتفكروا في الخالق فإنه لا يحيط به الفكرة )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r1.claim: The report from Ibn ʿAbbas says not to reflect on God, since you cannot grasp His true measure.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r1.anchor: تتفكروا في الله فإنكم لن تقدروا قدره ) , هذا هو المراد

BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r2.claim: He rejects interpreting the verse as union or any other heresy, and invokes God’s curse on its interpreter, defender, and silent supporter.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r2.anchor: فمن أول الآية باتحاد أو غير ذلك من الأغلحاد فعليه لعنة الله وعلى الذاب عنه والساكت عنه .

DURR-FULL:v7p661/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r3.claim: A prophetic report glosses the verse as forbidding speculation about God Himself.
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r3.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله {وأن إلى ربك المنتهى} قال: لا فكرة في الرب

DURR-FULL:v7p661/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r4.speaker: سفيان الثوري
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r4.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri likewise interprets the verse as no speculation about the Lord.
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r4.anchor: عن سفيان الثوري في قوله {وأن إلى ربك المنتهى} قال: لا فكرة في الرب

DURR-FULL:v7p661/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet telling people to reflect on creation rather than the Creator, since they cannot comprehend Him.
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: مر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على قوم يتفكرون في الله فقال: تفكروا في الخلق ولا تتفكروا في الخالق

DURR-FULL:v7p661/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r6.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r6.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet's warning to contemplate God's creation, not God, lest one perish.
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r6.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: تفكروا في خلق الله ولا تفكروا في الله فتهلكوا

DURR-FULL:v7p661/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r7.speaker: يونس بن ميسرة
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r7.claim: Yunus ibn Maysara reports that when companions discussed God's greatness, the Prophet repeated that they should not contemplate God but should contemplate the greatness of His creation.
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r7.anchor: عن يونس بن مسيرة قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أصحابه وهم يذكرون عظمة الله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v7p661/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r8.speaker: الحكم عن بعض أئمة الكوفة
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r8.claim: A report from a Kufa imam says companions reflected on the sun and creation; the Prophet directed them to creation and described a radiant land beyond the west, inhabited by creatures who do not know whether Adam or Iblis was created.
DURR-FULL:v7p661/r8.anchor: عن أبي أمية مولى شبرمة واسمه الحكم عن بعض أئمة الكوفة قال: قال ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r10.claim: The clause has the same position as verse 40 and may continue what was in Moses's and Abraham's scriptures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r10.anchor: القول في موقعها كالقول في موقع جملة { وأن سعيه سوف يرى } ( النجم : 40 ) سواء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r11.claim: The address “your Lord” shifts from third-person reference to second person without identifying the addressee, effectively saying that all return is to one's Lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r11.anchor: ويكون الخطاب في قوله : { إلى ربك } التفاتا من الغيبة إلى الخطاب والمخاطب غير معين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r12.claim: Ibrahim's declaration that he is going to his Lord may be a corresponding statement in his revealed teaching.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p139/r12.anchor: وقد يكون نظيرها من كلام إبراهيم ما حكاه الله عنه بقوله : { وقال إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين } ( الصافات : 99 ) .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r1.claim: These clauses are coordinated to the initially understood أن in verse 38; the majority read fatḥa, while Abū al-Sammāl reads kasra from verse 42 onward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r1.anchor: وقوله بعد ذلك وأنه، وأنه معطوف كل ذلك على أن المقدرة أولا في قوله: «أنه لا تزر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r2.speaker: أبو السمال قعنب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r2.claim: Abū al-Sammāl Qanab reads إن with kasra here and in what follows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p206#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال قعنب «وإن إلى ربك» بكسر الهمزة فيهما وفيما بعدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r7.claim: Al-muntahā may mean gathering and destination after death, an endpoint relative to worldly life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r7.anchor: و: المنتهى يحتمل أن يريد به الحشر، والمصير بعد الموت فهو منتهى بالإضافة إلى الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r8.claim: Alternatively it means Paradise or Hell as the absolute endpoint, with an omitted genitive for God’s punishment or mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد ب المنتهى: الجنة أو النار، فهو منتهى على الإطلاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r9.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r9.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports the Prophet’s statement that there is no speculation about the Lord.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r9.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب قال النبي عليه السلام في قوله تعالى: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى لا فكرة في الرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r10.speaker: أنس عن النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r10.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that when the Lord is mentioned, stop there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r10.anchor: وروى أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إذا ذكر الرب فانتهوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r11.claim: When companions said they were thinking about the Creator, the Prophet told them to reflect on creation, since thought cannot encompass the Creator.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207/r11.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما إلى أصحابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p82#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p82#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p82#3/r1.claim: The servants’ final destination and return are to their Lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p82#3/r1.anchor: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى أي منتهى العباد ومرجعهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p82#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p82#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p82#3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this entire passage is found in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p82#3/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج هذا كله في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r1.claim: The ultimate return is to God on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى [مخبرا] (1) {وأن إلى ربك المنتهى} أي: المعاد يوم القيامة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r2.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal told his people that the return is to God, ending either in Paradise or the Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r2.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون الأودي قال: قام فينا معاذ بن جبل فقال: يا بني أود، إني رسول الله إليكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r3.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet, the statement that there is no thinking about the Lord.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r3.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {وأن إلى ربك المنتهى} ، قال: لا فكرة في الرب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r4.claim: Al-Baghawi cites a raised report from Abu Hurayra: reflect on creation, not the Creator, because thought cannot encompass Him; Ibn Kathir says this wording is not preserved.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r4.anchor: قال البغوي: وهذا مثل ما روي عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا: "تفكروا في الخلق ولا تفكروا في الخالق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r5.claim: The sound hadith says Satan asks who created this and that until he asks who created your Lord; one should seek God's protection and stop.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r5.anchor: وإنما الذي في الصحيح: "يأتي الشيطان أحدكم فيقول: من خلق كذا؟ من خلق كذا؟ حتى يقول: من خلق ربك؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r6.claim: A report in the Sunan says to contemplate God's creations, not His essence, and describes an angel whose distance from earlobe to shoulder is three hundred years.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث الآخر الذي في السنن: "تفكروا في مخلوقات الله، ولا تفكروا (6) في ذات الله

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r10.claim: Al-muntahā is the destination where action ceases.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r10.anchor: والمنتهى: المصير إلى حيث ينقطع العمل عنده

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r19.claim: Views make God the final judge, the endpoint of reward or punishment, the source of grace and hopes, or the limit of thought beyond which one must not speculate about God.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r19.anchor: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى أي: المرجع إلى الموضع، الذي لا ينفذ فيه حكم أحد إلا حكمه تعالى، وقيل: إلى ثوابه وعقابه ينتهي الخلق

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r20.speaker: أنس
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r20.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction to stop when God is mentioned.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r20.anchor: وروى أنس أن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: إذا ذكر الرب فانتهوا

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r21.claim: A report instructs people to reflect on creation, not the Creator, since thought cannot encompass Him; no grading is stated.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r21.anchor: وروي: تفكروا في الخلق ولا تفكروا في الخالق، فإنه لا يحيط به الفكرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r10.claim: Read with fatḥa it says all this is in the scriptures; read with kasra it begins a new sentence, as with what follows.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r10.anchor: قرىء بالفتح على معنى : أن هذا كله في الصحف ، وبالكسر على الابتداء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r11.claim: المنتهى means the end: creation ends with God and returns to Him, as in 35:18.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r11.anchor: والمنتهى : مصدر بمعنى الانتهاء ، أي : ينتهي إليه الخلق

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r1.claim: One possible meaning is that after death, people return to their Lord, their ultimate destination.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r1.anchor: إلى إعادتكم لربكم بعد موتكم يكون منتهاكم

MUQATIL:53:33-42/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r10.claim: All knowledge ultimately ends with the Lord.
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r10.anchor: { وأن إلى ربك المنتهى } [آية: 42] ينتهي إليه بعلمه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#5/r1.claim: These statements occur in the earlier scriptures; al-muntahā is a verbal noun meaning the end, where creatures arrive and to which they return, as the verse says, “To Allah is the final return.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#5/r1.anchor: هذاكله في الصحف الاولى والمنتهى مصدر بمعنى الانتهاء اى ينتهى اليه الخلق ويرجعون اليه كقوله ولاى الله المصير

QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r4.claim: The final return is to God, who rewards and punishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r4.anchor: أي المرجع والمرد والمصير فيعاقب ويثيب

QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r5.claim: Another view says favor begins with God and security ultimately ends with Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r5.anchor: وقيل: منه ابتداء المنة وإليه انتهاء الأمان

QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r6.claim: A report from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says there is no speculation about the Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r6.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r7.speaker: أنس عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r7.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet's instruction: when God is mentioned, stop.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r7.anchor: وعن أنس: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi links this to the hadith that Satan asks who created the Lord, at which point one should seek refuge and stop.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r8.anchor: فإذا بلغ ذلك فليستعذ بالله ولينته

QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r9.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r9.claim: A poem counsels against speculating about God's essence and urges reflection on created works.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:40-42/r9.anchor: ولا تفكرن في ذي العلا عز وجهه فإنك تردى إن فعلت وتخذل
